subject.title: [Bug] Command validation bypass on multi-line tool calls in parser

question: Does a concrete current-main payload demonstrate that repaired multiline arguments cross tool-schema and execution-policy checks, warranting private advisory handling and a boundary fix?
rationale: Only a trusted security reviewer can safely evaluate an exploit payload and determine whether disclosure should move to a private GHSA or whether the report should be downgraded as non-reproducible.

options.title: Request private boundary proof
options.body: Keep the issue security-routed while asking the reporter to submit a redacted payload and end-to-end trace through the repository's private security process.

options.title: Downgrade after source audit
options.body: Remove the security signal only if a complete audit confirms every relevant dispatch path structurally validates arguments and enforces execution policy.

recommendation.title: Request private boundary proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue security-routed while asking the reporter to submit a redacted payload and end-to-end trace through the repository's private security process.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work directly owns multiline command extraction and script-preflight hardening in the central shell execution boundary.
